clue.text: Anything on Friday is stressful

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: FR is the standard abbreviation for Friday
an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: Whatever happens at the end of the working week turns out to be stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the day first: FR then AUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraught situation is full of tension and anxiety, a close synonym.

clue.text: Nipper, one who’s mastered the violin has to grumble after …

explanation.surface: A master violinist has cause for complaint, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipper is anything that pinches, here a crustacean with one huge claw.
explanation.definitionFit: The male of this crab has one oversized claw that pinches, so it is a creature that nips.

clue.text: … violin maker’s answer on dull one

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a matt finish is dull, not glossy; also spelt mat

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a violin maker answers a dull question.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated craftsmen of string instruments in the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: State who might be on my mind as a singer?

definitions.text: State who might be on my mind as a singer?

blocks.clueFragment: State who might be on my mind as a singer?
blocks.note: surface reading: a vocalist preoccupied with someone

blocks.clueFragment: State who might be on my mind as a singer?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a US state named in the title of a Ray Charles hit, and also a woman's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' hints the state is also a person; the song title puts the state on the singer's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: This southern US state shares its name with a woman's given name and features in a classic song title.

clue.text: Upset women leave forgotten northern play with male leads

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoyed actresses quit a forgotten northern drama in which only men star.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's early comedy centres on Valentine and Proteus, two friends, so its leading roles are both men.

clue.text: Approach sheep seen during ramble

indicators.note: something seen during an event is in the middle of it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: to ramble is to wander off or stray
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A walker on a country ramble comes across some sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Teg is a dialect and crossword word for a sheep in its second year; 'Approach' reads as a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a planned way of tackling a problem, the same as an overall plan of attack.

clue.text: Indignant sons joined forces

blocks.note: S for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Angry sons band together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up and angry about some perceived wrong is the colloquial sense, matching indignant.

clue.text: Famous Roman wanting ancient region of Iraq overthrown

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, which in a down clue means read from the bottom

blocks.note: Sumer was the early civilisation of southern Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A Roman general covets a Mesopotamian land after its fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Remus and his twin Romulus were the legendary founders of Rome, raised by a she-wolf.

clue.text: Reasonable state of anger at end of game

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A reasonable player still loses their temper at the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and restrained in behaviour, which is being sensible and reasonable.

clue.text: Silly mistake introducing Irish high-level browser

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: IR is an abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A blunder involving an Irish web browser at the top level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' sounds like software; here it is an animal that browses on leaves, high in the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The tallest land animal feeds by browsing leaves from the tops of trees, so it browses at a high level.

clue.text: A measure of power returning to old capital

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters are written in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the watt is the SI unit of power
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A unit of electrical power is restored to its old level.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, so it is a specific example of a capital.

clue.text: Get damp over outside of wet weather shoe

indicators.note: over in a down clue means flipped upwards, so the word is read backwards
outside of means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to ret flax is to soak it, so ret means get soaked

explanation.surface: A shoe for wet weather is getting soaked through.
explanation.walkthrough: RET is an old word for soaking flax or hemp; reversed, it splits round the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, called a sneaker in American English.

clue.text: Habit of speech used by a duke

explanation.surface: A duke has a verbal tic in his speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used by' puts the speech after A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependency, an entrenched habit that is hard to break.

clue.text: Experts showing fiasco on aid abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests wandering far and wide, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Specialists reveal the mess made of foreign aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Aficionados are keen and knowledgeable enthusiasts, close in sense to connoisseurs or specialists.

clue.text: Try to remember woman involved with money orders

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up together, so the letters get mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman gets caught up in a scheme with postal money orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on one's memory is to call up stored recollections, which is making an effort to recall.

clue.text: Former politician’s good with greeting

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A retired politician is good at shaking hands and saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement, and Indira and Rajiv Gandhi were later prime ministers: past political figures.

clue.text: Unwell after a beer with papa, drunk turned to whisky — admit that’s hard to take

indicators.note: after means following, so the word before it is placed behind the pieces named next
turned means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: bitter is a British style of beer
Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet
Whisky is W in the phonetic alphabet
to allow a claim is to admit it

explanation.surface: Dad, already the worse for beer, moves on to whisky and pays for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British amber beer; papa and whisky are NATO alphabet words. 'Turned to' means reversed and placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an unpleasant fact one must accept, which is something difficult to swallow or accept.

clue.text: Perjury is brief but not fine

indicators.note: 'but not' asks for the first word minus the thing that follows

blocks.note: as in a flying visit, a brief one
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A short false statement under oath still counts as perjury, whatever the fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is the hard step: think of a flying visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is the crime of telling untruths under oath, so the noun for telling untruths fits.

clue.text: Men being silly fools, mostly all together

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
silly behaviour is disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A group of men acting the fool as a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English to mean as a whole group, everyone at once.

clue.text: Lie attached to account given by current mathematician

blocks.note: a fib is a small lie
ACC is an abbreviation for account
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A dishonest story about a current account comes from a numbers man.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo of Pisa, known by this nickname, was the medieval Italian mathematician behind the famous number sequence.

clue.text: Embarrassed about English pamphlet being withdrawn

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the others

blocks.note: a tract is a short polemical pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone is ashamed that their English pamphlet has been pulled from circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement that has been retracted has been taken back, which is a passive sense matching withdrawn.

clue.text: Oven that’s too darn complicated

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An exasperated cook finds the new oven far too fiddly to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandoor is a clay cylindrical cooking device from South Asia, so it is a kind of oven.

clue.text: Chemical spy used against soldiers

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A spy employed to work against enemy troops, perhaps with poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used against' places the spy next to the soldiers, which come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added in a laboratory to cause or detect a reaction, so it is one kind of chemical.

clue.text: Republican has to draw out Democrat in a smaller state

blocks.note: to educe is to draw out or elicit

explanation.surface: A Republican must lure a Democrat out in a small US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests American politics but means condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reduced has been made smaller, so it is now in a diminished condition.

clue.text: Rule from abroad shunned by FO

indicators.note: being shunned means being left out, so the named letters are removed

blocks.note: foreign describes what comes from another country

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office refuses to accept rule by an outside power.
explanation.walkthrough: FO is the Foreign Office, Britain's diplomatic ministry, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period or act of ruling, and to reign is to rule.

clue.text: Manage getting out of bed for start of delivery

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to get out of bed in time for a morning parcel delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's delivery begins with the approach to the crease, which is why the definition works.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-up is the bowler's approach before releasing the ball, the opening phase of each ball bowled.

clue.text: Poet needing to promote stock

blocks.note: to push a product is to promote it

explanation.surface: A poet has to market his merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like goods for sale but means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pushkin is Russia's great national poet, author of Eugene Onegin.

clue.text: Need exit built both sides of parking to be appropriate

indicators.note: something built is constructed from parts, so the letters are assembled in a new order
the rearranged letters sit on either side, enclosing the next item

blocks.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A car park needs an exit at each end to be suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expedient is convenient and suitable for the purpose, even if not strictly principled.

clue.text: Flower beginning to turn on unwanted plant

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted

explanation.surface: A bloom starts to wilt beside a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: something that flows, a river, here the one on the England-Scotland border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river forming part of the Anglo-Scottish border, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Returned cotton fabric, concerned with how lords are dressed

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: the cotton cloth used for jeans

explanation.surface: Cotton cloth sent back by peers who expect finer clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers' ceremonial robes are trimmed with white stoat fur, so lords in their robes are fur-trimmed in this way.

clue.text: Moorcock mostly shot for fine skin

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
shot means ruined or broken, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; a moorcock is a male red grouse

explanation.surface: A grouse mostly shot on the moor for its fine plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a soft, fine goatskin leather used for bookbinding, so a quality skin.

clue.text: What keeps up publishers’ output schedules, mostly to assist frequency

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for frequency

explanation.surface: A publisher's print schedules mostly help to keep the presses busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps up' means holds aloft, as a shelf supports volumes, not maintains.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishers produce volumes, and this piece of furniture holds them up off the floor in rows.

clue.text: Book for lido? Not right day

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Choosing a book for the swimming pool, but it's not the right day for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool. Remove R and D from 'for lido'.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a large-format book made from sheets folded once, so a type of volume.

clue.text: Material dug up, bobby’s got it inside where bodies were burnt

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a bobby and a copper are both slang for a police officer; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A police officer recovers evidence buried at a cremation site.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby is British slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: This brassy yellow mineral is the main ore of copper and is extracted by mining, so it is mined material.

clue.text: Stop press conference, for example

definitions.note: read as two words, PR event

blocks.note: first meaning: to hinder or block
second meaning: split as PR (public relations) plus a word for an occasion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop press' looks like a newspaper phrase; split it, and a press conference is an example of a public-relations occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening, and a press briefing is one kind of publicity occasion.

clue.text: America writer a superhero: admirer releasing book

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: the Norse god appears as a Marvel superhero

explanation.surface: An American author is an admirer of a comic-book superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America writer' reads as American writer; the clue appears to be printed with 'America' for 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau wrote Walden and was a leading nineteenth-century American essayist.

clue.text: Early intelligence going to English king today left border

explanation.surface: Advance intelligence reports an English king crossing the border today.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing about something before it happens is information obtained in advance, so early intelligence.

clue.text: One sending out jets to shoot warplane

blocks.note: to fire a gun is to shoot
a fighter is a combat aircraft

explanation.surface: A command to shoot down an enemy jet fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jets' suggests aircraft, which fits the surface; it means streams of water from a hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tackling blazes directs streams of water from hoses, so they send out jets of water.

clue.text: Tasty food shop, overflowing but needing work

indicators.note: needing here means lacking, so the following item is taken out

explanation.surface: A busy delicatessen is overflowing with customers but short of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is delicious has a very pleasant taste, a straightforward synonym for flavoursome.

clue.text: Audience’s left outside following problem for actors

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the next

standard abbreviation, as in p. 4 f.

explanation.definitionFit: Nervous dread before performing in front of people is a well-known affliction of performers.

clue.text: Tsar’s family roam about some weeks soon after the revolution

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.clueFragment: some weeks soon after the revolution
blocks.note: the month following October, when the Russian Revolution took place

explanation.walkthrough: The 1917 Bolshevik rising is called the October Revolution, so the month soon after is November.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanov dynasty ruled Russia from 1613 until 1917, so it was the tsars' ruling house.

clue.text: Revolting cup holds very little in

indicators.note: a cup that holds something has it inside, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: a mug is a drinking cup

explanation.surface: A disgusting cup has only a drop left inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' suggests disgusting; here it means rising in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors or soldiers rising against their officers are in revolt, the participle sense of revolting.

clue.text: Where to apply the acne cream immediately

definitions.text: Where to apply the acne cream

blocks.clueFragment: Where to apply the acne cream
blocks.note: first meaning: literally on the pimple itself
second meaning: an idiom for at once, without delay

explanation.walkthrough: The skincare instruction is read literally; the second definition is the everyday idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at once, there and then, while literally it locates a pimple.

clue.text: Toaster’s empty, meal’s not begun — this could hit one hard

explanation.walkthrough: A truncheon is a police baton, called a nightstick in the US.

clue.text: Wrong hexadecimal symbol used in top academic computer

explanation.walkthrough: Both F and C are hexadecimal digits, so swapping one for the other is the 'wrong' symbol.

clue.text: Work in proper atmosphere

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: letters found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Getting work done needs the right environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a musical work, a staged composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is the Latin plural of opus, and a single opera is a dramatic musical composition, a work.

clue.text: Is preoccupied, missing nine Roman goddesses of destiny

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters are taken out

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with tracking down the missing ninth of a group of deities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' fits the surface and also points to Roman numerals for nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The three Fates, the Parcae in Rome, spun, measured and cut the thread of every life.

clue.text: What to do after dropping off small saddle

definitions.text: What to do after dropping off

blocks.note: to saddle someone with a task is to lumber them with it

explanation.surface: A rider dismounts and takes the small saddle off the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' suggests unloading, but it means falling asleep.

clue.text: Tell what can happen in a close election

definitions.text: what can happen in a close election

blocks.note: first meaning: narrate or relate a story

blocks.clueFragment: what can happen in a close election
blocks.note: second meaning: a second tally of votes

explanation.walkthrough: One meaning is the verb, stressed on the second syllable; the other is the noun, stressed on the first.

clue.text: Fuel tube in heart of reactor get to eaten away

blocks.note: a reactor's core is its centre

clue.text: Building over a street hard beside Sussex river

blocks.note: O for over, as in cricket scoring
H for hard, as on pencils
the Ouse flows through Lewes in Sussex

explanation.surface: A building bridging a street stands next to a river in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Oast houses, with cowled roofs for drying hops, are a feature of Kent and Sussex, so the river suits the scene.

clue.text: Arrogance of hospital director

blocks.note: an auteur is a film director with a strong personal style

clue.text: Smuggler initially gets us nicked by Bow Street policeman

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: the Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force

explanation.surface: A smuggler gets the gang arrested by an old-time London constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies to three words, not just one.

clue.text: Ring artist producing impossible illusion

explanation.surface: An artist on the phone makes an impossible optical trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful hope or fantasy that cannot be realised, named after the mythical hybrid monster.

clue.text: I had that thing about Oscar being a fool

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the following letter

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone admits they once won an Oscar and made a fool of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, so a straightforward synonym for a dimwit or simpleton.

clue.text: Sore heads on utterly lairy chaps, extremely ratted

clue.text: Church, trendy, with a service for teatime, perhaps

clue.text: Novel type of hat

second meaning: a soft felt hat with an indented crown

clue.text: Plant that has beautiful ladies weeping

blocks.note: a wound weeps or oozes blood

explanation.surface: A flower whose drooping blooms look like lovely women in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: This amaranth with long drooping crimson tassels is a garden flower, so a plant.

clue.text: Judge — one who’s pulling back, half-heartedly

explanation.definitionFit: To regard someone as guilty is to consider or deem them so, which is a sense of judging.

clue.text: Rent isle going free in south-eastern Ireland

indicators.note: letters set free can scatter and land in a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is the Irish province covering the east and south-east, including Dublin and Wexford.

clue.text: Justify time on western Scottish isle

indicators.note: 'on' means added after, so the piece named first is placed at the end

blocks.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: Can one defend spending time on a western Scottish island?
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the time after the rest, as in a down clue's stacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant an action is to provide grounds that make it reasonable, so to justify it.
